name: Responsible AI and regulatory compliance
description: Meeting ethical and legal duties for AI systems: disclosure, audit trails, data minimisation and privacy impact assessments, under the EU AI Act, the NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.
l1: Knows the EU AI Act tiers and current dates, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001
l2: Implements Article 50 disclosure, trace-based audit logs and PII minimisation
l3: Classifies use cases (e.g. Annex III) and maps controls to Articles 12 and 14 and to AI RMF functions; runs DPIAs on agent data flows
l4: Runs an ISO 42001-style management system across an agent portfolio; tracks moving regulation such as the Omnibus and CAISI outputs

name: Business and problem discovery
description: Finding the real problem inside a customer's business: how it earns, spends and carries risk, what users actually do, and what a correct answer looks like.
l1: Explains how a customer's business earns revenue, incurs cost and carries risk; can tell a requested feature from the problem behind it
l2: Interviews users, observes the work and examines the evidence; states the underlying problem, and what a correct answer looks like in the customer's terms; records where each requirement came from
l3: Leads discovery in an unfamiliar organisation; traces a problem to its root cause and gets the stakeholders' agreement to the conclusions; catches a solution that is technically valid but commercially wrong; coaches others in discovery
l4: Sets a discovery method that other teams adopt; is consulted on a domain's problems beyond their own engagements
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.1); description: drafted for the graph

name: Process analysis and task allocation
description: Mapping a workflow as it is really done and deciding which tasks go to fixed code, a model, an agent or a person.
l1: Knows the parts of a workflow (activities, hand-offs, approvals, exceptions), and that fixed rules, a model, an agent and a person each suit different tasks
l2: Maps a workflow as it is actually done, in a process model others can read, with its exceptions and bottlenecks; assigns each task to code, a model, an agent or a person, with approval points
l3: Decomposes a process that crosses teams; sets out alternative designs and whether each is feasible; justifies the degree of autonomy at each step with evidence of cost and error; reviews others' allocations
l4: Sets the organisation's method for deciding what is automated and what stays with people
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.2); description: drafted for the graph

name: Customer systems and enterprise integration
description: Fitting a solution into a customer's existing systems: their applications, data flows, identity and owners, and integration across APIs, files, feeds and legacy systems.
l1: Knows the common enterprise systems (ERP, CRM, data warehouse, identity provider) and the ways they exchange data (API, file, SFTP, database, queue)
l2: Maps a customer's systems, their owners and their data flows; builds and tests an integration on the customer's own infrastructure, alongside their engineers, that handles authentication, rate limits, retries and duplicates
l3: Decides where a new solution fits in the existing estate; designs integration across legacy and modern systems with reconciliation; assesses the integration risks; works inside the customer's network limits and security review
l4: Sets reference integration architectures reused across customers
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.3); description: drafted for the graph

name: Platform fit, configuration and reuse
description: Knowing the deployed platform well enough to choose configuration or custom code, and turning what works into reusable parts and product feedback.
l1: Knows the deployed platform's capabilities, limits, extension points and security model
l2: Meets a requirement by configuration where that is enough and by custom code where it is not; knows what each costs to run
l3: Separates a general product gap from a local requirement; turns a working pattern into a tool, playbook or building block that others use; takes field evidence, including where the model succeeds and fails, back to the product team
l4: Shapes the product roadmap from field evidence; builds components adopted across customers
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.4); description: drafted for the graph

name: Prototyping and assumption testing
description: Narrow prototypes that test the riskiest assumptions first, and knowing what a successful demonstration still leaves unproven.
l1: Knows what a prototype is for, and how a demonstration differs from a production system
l2: Builds a narrow prototype that tests one named assumption (feasibility, data availability or usefulness) and reports what it showed
l3: Orders experiments by risk; states what a successful demonstration leaves unproven; checks that architectural assumptions survive implementation
l4: Sets how an organisation takes work from prototype to production, adopted beyond their own team
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.5); description: drafted for the graph

name: Delivery and scope management
description: Getting an engagement delivered: scoping, sequencing, estimating, clearing blockers and making trade-offs between scope, speed and quality.
l1: Knows scope, estimates, dependencies and blockers
l2: Scopes, sequences and estimates their own work; tracks dependencies; reports progress, risks and issues; raises and removes blockers early
l3: Owns the delivery of an engagement from first prototype to stable production: writes the scope of work and the plan, delivers in increments, manages risks and dependencies, controls scope, and gets the trade-offs between scope, speed and quality stated and agreed
l4: Sets the delivery method used across engagements
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.6); description: drafted for the graph

name: Stakeholder communication and decision ownership
description: Explaining technical decisions to executives, operators, developers and security teams, and settling who decides what.
l1: Knows the audiences on an engagement (executives, operators, developers, security) and what each needs to hear
l2: Explains a technical decision to a non-technical audience; records who owns each decision
l3: Brings executives, operators and security teams through a disagreement to a decision; coaches others
l4: Advises customer executives across several engagements; sets the communication practice other teams follow
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.7); description: drafted for the graph

name: Adoption, handover and operational ownership
description: Getting a deployed system used and owned: training, runbooks, a named operating owner and the changes in habit that adoption needs.
l1: Knows that a deployed system is not yet an adopted one; knows runbooks and operational ownership
l2: Trains users, writes the runbook, agrees with the customer's operators what must be true before they accept the system, and hands it to a named owner who can operate it
l3: Designs adoption into daily work, including the incentives and habits that block it; works out how the change affects operational work and adjusts the change plan from feedback; leaves the customer able to diagnose and fix production failures without the engagement team
l4: Sets adoption and handover practice across engagements, including the move from engagement delivery to the customer's own operation
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.8); description: drafted for the graph

name: Outcome measurement and delivery economics
description: Showing what a deployment changed and what it costs: baselines, outcome measures, total cost of ownership and the build, buy or extend decision.
l1: Knows baselines, outcome measures (cycle time, accuracy, manual effort, cost, risk) and total cost of ownership
l2: Sets a baseline before delivery, agrees the measures and how they will be tracked, and measures the change after it (adoption in production and the effect on the workflow); counts maintenance and human review in the cost
l3: Builds the return case for an engagement (cost, benefit, impact and risk of each option; cost for each successfully completed task; support burden; the long-term cost of customer-specific work); compares the result with what the case predicted; decides build, buy or extend
l4: Sets how the organisation measures and prices delivered outcomes
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B9.9); description: drafted for the graph

name: AI disclosure and use boundaries
description: Being open about what AI did: disclosing and citing AI's part in the work, and keeping within the AI rules of clients, professional bodies, publishers and platforms.
l1: Knows the principles of responsible AI use in their field: accuracy, disclosure, privacy, education and compliance
l2: Discloses where AI materially shaped the work and records which AI tools were used; cites an AI response where its words are kept; never presents AI-generated or AI-altered material as evidence
l3: Writes an AI-use statement for a project or product saying what agents did and what people verified; checks the AI rules of clients, credentialing bodies, publishers and platforms before delivering
l4: Contributes to AI guidelines or position statements that a professional body, society or coalition publishes
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B6.5), the agentic field's shared Mandatory wording; description: drafted for the graph

name: Privacy and data protection in AI use
description: Controlling what reaches a model: keeping personal and confidential data out of prompts, checking providers' data terms, and automatic redaction and release checks.
l1: Knows that data sent to a model provider can leave their control, and what a provider's data terms cover
l2: Keeps personal and confidential data out of prompts unless it is permitted; checks a provider's data terms before sending records
l3: Builds redaction and release checks into the workflow and enforces the policy automatically
l4: Designs privacy arrangements for AI use that projects or organisations the person does not run adopt
source: L1-L4: chan-afse.md (B6.6), the agentic field's shared Mandatory wording; description: drafted for the graph

name: Verification of agent output
description: Not taking an agent's word for it: checking output against the source, a test or an independent check before relying on it.
l1: Knows that an agent saying work is done or correct is a claim, not proof, and that models produce fluent errors
l2: Checks agent output against the source, a test or an independent check before relying on it; records what was checked
l3: Builds verification into the work (independent reviewers or tests, checking rates set by risk); measures the error that gets through; guides others
l4: Sets verification standards adopted beyond their own team or project
